description: A single-panel schematic (line drawing, no micrograph, no axes, no scale bar) illustrating the deformation-zone geometry of a cylindrical compression specimen. The specimen is drawn in longitudinal section, its outline slightly barrelled, with a vertical dash-dot centre line and a horizontal dash-dot centre line dividing it into quadrants. Dashed curved lines partition the interior into three regions whose numbers are printed twice by symmetry: "1" appears in the top-centre and bottom-centre near the loading surfaces (the caption calls this the difficult deformation zone), "2" appears at the far left and far right ends adjacent to the horizontal centre line (small deformation zone), and "3" appears in the central horizontal band of the specimen (large deformation zone). On the right-hand side a bold downward arrow is labelled "Loading force P", indicating that the load is applied parallel to the specimen axis. The figure demonstrates that compression testing produces a non-uniform stress/strain field inside a specimen, and defines the three sampling locations (1, 2, 3) whose microstructures are subsequently examined. No numeric values, coordinates or units are printed anywhere in the panel.

observations.observation: The figure is a purely schematic line drawing of a barrelled cylindrical compression specimen in longitudinal section; it contains no micrograph, no axes, no scale bar and no numerical data.

Dashed curved boundary lines divide the specimen interior into three regions, and the index numbers ('1', '2', '3') are each printed twice, placed symmetrically about both the vertical and horizontal centre lines.
Region '1' is located at the top-centre and bottom-centre of the section, immediately beneath and above the flat loading surfaces.
Region '2' is located at the extreme left and right ends of the specimen, adjacent to the horizontal dash-dot centre line.
Region '3' occupies the central horizontal band of the specimen, lying between regions 1 and 2.
A bold downward arrow on the right side of the drawing is labelled 'Loading force P', indicating uniaxial load applied parallel to the specimen axis.
The caption states that zone 1 is the difficult deformation zone, zone 2 the small deformation zone and zone 3 the large deformation zone.

The citing text states that friction between the contact surface and the pressure head during compression causes an unevenly distributed stress field, producing the different deformation zones shown in the section parallel to the loading direction.
The citing text states that the specimens for the schematic are FeeMneAleC steel deformed under hot-deformation conditions (Gleeble-3500 simulator).

The citing text states that the microstructures of the three deformation zones defined in this figure are subsequently characterised (in Fig. 9), with labels 1, 2 and 3 in Fig. 9 corresponding to the difficult, small and large deformation zones respectively.
No numeric values, dimensions, temperatures, strain rates or units are printed on this figure.

subfigures.description: Line-drawing schematic of a cylindrical compression specimen in longitudinal section, with dashed curved boundaries dividing the interior into three numbered zones: 1 (top and bottom centre, near the loading surfaces), 2 (left and right ends), and 3 (central band). A downward arrow at the right is labelled 'Loading force P'. Vertical and horizontal dash-dot centre lines are drawn.
